P1 registered a bundle and P2 proved the object inside it behaves. This
is the step where it stops being a row in its own tab and becomes
something `/algorithms` lists and a simulation can name — which is the
whole point of the import path, and the part that would be easiest to
declare done while the plugin remained unreachable.

The end-to-end case drives a real episode: the API builds the stack, the
lane starts a worker process, the loop binds the channel seam and steps
the plugin every tick. Nothing here is stubbed, because a stub would
prove the catalogue entry exists rather than that it runs.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from conftest import ADMIN, auth_headers
from test_api_plugin_conformance import WORKING_PLANNER, import_probe, probe_manifest

STACK_ID = "astar+org.vinai.vfh-plus"


@pytest.fixture
def admin(client):
    return auth_headers(client, ADMIN)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _clean_catalogue():
    """The runtime catalogue is process-global, so a test that registers
    a plugin would otherwise leak it into the next one."""
    from planbench_benchmark.registry import clear_external

    clear_external()
    yield
    clear_external()


def algorithms(client, headers) -> dict[str, dict]:
    return {row["id"]: row for row in client.get("/api/v1/algorithms", headers=headers).json()}


class TestARunnablePluginJoinsTheCatalogue:
    def test_it_is_listed_beside_the_built_ins(self, client, admin):
        import_probe(client, admin, WORKING_PLANNER)
        catalogue = algorithms(client, admin)
        assert STACK_ID in catalogue
        assert "astar+dwa" in catalogue, "built-ins must not be displaced by the second source"

    def test_what_it_declares_is_what_is_published(self, client, admin):
        """Nothing inferred from the plugin id: the observation class
        comes from the declared requirements, the schema from the
        manifest, the global-path flag from the manifest."""
        import_probe(client, admin, WORKING_PLANNER)
        entry = algorithms(client, admin)[STACK_ID]
        assert entry["local_controller"] == "org.vinai.vfh-plus"
        assert entry["global_planner"] == "astar"
        assert entry["local_observation_class"] == "lidar_only"
        assert entry["requires_global_path"] is True
        assert entry["requires_model"] is False
        assert entry["benchmarkable"] is True

    def test_it_can_be_fetched_by_id_like_any_other(self, client, admin):
        import_probe(client, admin, WORKING_PLANNER)
        response = client.get(f"/api/v1/algorithms/{STACK_ID}", headers=admin)
        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.json()["id"] == STACK_ID


class TestOnlyWhatEarnedItIsOffered:
    def test_a_plugin_that_failed_conformance_is_not_in_the_catalogue(self, client, admin):
        crashing = "class Planner:\n    def reset(self, r): pass\n"
        body = import_probe(client, admin, crashing).json()
        assert body["validation_status"] == "failed"
        assert STACK_ID not in algorithms(client, admin)

    def test_a_plugin_that_could_not_be_run_is_not_offered_either(self, client, admin):
        """`structural` means unverified, not verified-good. Offering it
        would put a candidate on the leaderboard on the strength of
        having been readable."""
        manifest = probe_manifest(
            requirements={"all_of": ["planbench://channel/static-costmap@1"]}
        )
        body = import_probe(client, admin, WORKING_PLANNER, manifest=manifest).json()
        assert body["validation_status"] == "structural"
        assert STACK_ID not in algorithms(client, admin)

    def test_disabling_one_withdraws_it_from_the_catalogue(self, client, admin):
        bundle_id = import_probe(client, admin, WORKING_PLANNER).json()["id"]
        assert STACK_ID in algorithms(client, admin)
        client.patch(
            f"/api/v1/algorithms/plugins/{bundle_id}", json={"status": "disabled"}, headers=admin
        )
        assert STACK_ID not in algorithms(client, admin)

    def test_re_enabling_it_puts_it_back(self, client, admin):
        bundle_id = import_probe(client, admin, WORKING_PLANNER).json()["id"]
        client.patch(
            f"/api/v1/algorithms/plugins/{bundle_id}", json={"status": "disabled"}, headers=admin
        )
        client.patch(
            f"/api/v1/algorithms/plugins/{bundle_id}", json={"status": "active"}, headers=admin
        )
        assert STACK_ID in algorithms(client, admin)


class TestItActuallyDrivesAnEpisode:
    def test_a_simulation_runs_the_imported_controller(
        self, client, admin, created_map, created_scenario
    ):
        """The end of the path An asked for: somebody who is not a
        developer uploads a bundle and the platform simulates with it.

        A worker process starts, the loop binds the channel seam it found
        on the controller, and the plugin answers every tick.
        """
        import_probe(client, admin, WORKING_PLANNER)
        created = client.post(
            "/api/v1/simulations",
            json={
                "map_id": created_map["id"],
                "scenario_id": created_scenario["id"],
                "algorithm": STACK_ID,
            },
            headers=admin,
        )
        assert created.status_code == 201, created.text

        run = client.post(f"/api/v1/simulations/{created.json()['id']}/run", headers=admin)
        assert run.status_code == 200, run.text
        body = run.json()
        assert body["state"] == "finished"
        # The probe drives forward at a constant speed and never turns,
        # so it is not expected to reach the goal — only to have been
        # asked, tick after tick, and to have answered.
        assert body["result"]["steps"] > 5
        assert len(body["result"]["trajectory"]) > 5

    def test_an_unimported_plugin_id_is_still_refused(self, client, admin, created_map, created_scenario):
        response = client.post(
            "/api/v1/simulations",
            json={
                "map_id": created_map["id"],
                "scenario_id": created_scenario["id"],
                "algorithm": "astar+org.nobody.never-imported",
            },
            headers=admin,
        )
        assert response.status_code == 422


class TestTheTwoObservationTablesAgree:
    def test_the_inverse_mapping_matches_the_forward_one(self):
        """`plugin_stacks` states the requirements-to-class mapping in
        the opposite direction from `legacy_plugins`. Deriving one from
        the other at import time would make a typo in either look like
        agreement, so they are written twice and compared here."""
        from planbench_benchmark.legacy_plugins import _CLASS_REQUIREMENTS
        from planbench_benchmark.plugin_stacks import CLASS_FOR_REQUIREMENTS

        for observation_class, requirements in _CLASS_REQUIREMENTS.items():
            key = frozenset(requirements)
            if key not in CLASS_FOR_REQUIREMENTS:
                # `full_static_map+human_states` shares its requirement
                # set with `human_states`: the difference is the map,
                # which no requirement token carries. A plugin declaring
                # only human states is the sensing case, so that is the
                # one the inverse names.
                assert observation_class == "full_static_map+human_states"
                continue
            assert CLASS_FOR_REQUIREMENTS[key] == observation_class

# Đường vào UI cho thuật toán ngoài — P0 đến P4

**Ngày:** 2026-08-24 · **Nhánh:** `tongduyan_plugin-import-ui` (tạo mới, **không đụng `main`**)

| Commit | Phase |
|---|---|
| `23bc7e6` | P0 — threat model |
| `4e4c126` | P1 — nhận và đăng ký bundle |

| `e6544de` | P3 — catalogue hợp nhất, chạy được episode thật |

---

## 1. Kết quả: người dùng không phải dev làm được gì

Đăng nhập bằng tài khoản admin → **Models → tab "Nhập thuật toán"** → chọn tệp
`.zip` → bấm nhập. Sau đó:

- Server đọc mục lục zip, parse `plugin.json`, **không giải nén, không import**.
- Nếu manifest hợp lệ: giải nén vào thư mục riêng, nạp plugin trong **tiến trình
  con**, chạy bộ conformance của SDK.
- Nếu plugin hành xử đúng: nó xuất hiện trong `GET /algorithms` cạnh
  `astar+dwa`, và **chạy mô phỏng được ngay** dưới tên `astar+<plugin-id>`.

Không chạm terminal dòng nào. Có test đầu-cuối chứng minh: upload qua HTTP →
tạo simulation → chạy → episode có `steps > 5`, tiến trình worker thật sự chạy.

---

## 2. Hai quyết định An chốt trong phiên, và vì sao chúng đổi plan

| Câu hỏi | Chốt |
|---|---|
| UI nhận gì | Bundle `.zip` **có code** |
| Lane | **Subprocess bắt buộc** |

Quyết định cũ ngày 20-08 là "chỉ nhận `plugin.json`". Nó không đạt được mục tiêu
An nêu, vì manifest khai entry point chứ không chứa code — người dùng vẫn cần một
dev cài `planner.py` lên máy sweep.

Và lý do đứng sau quyết định cũ — "không đưa code lạ lên máy chủ" — **đã không
còn mô tả đúng hệ thống**: `_build_ppo` gọi `PPO.load()` unpickle checkpoint
người dùng upload, ngay trong tiến trình API. Nhận bundle code không mở ra lớp
rủi ro mới; nó dùng lại lớp đã chấp nhận, và đặt plugin vào lane cô lập tốt hơn
PPO đang có.

---

## 3. Từng phase đã làm gì

### P0 — `docs/plugin_import_security.md`

Threat model một trang, không code. Nội dung chịu lực:

- **Thứ tự** các bước, và bước nào còn từ chối được (mọi bước trước khi conformance chạy).
- **Quyền thật của code**: subprocess = cô lập crash và interpreter, **không phải
  sandbox**. Worker thừa kế environment, `PYTHONPATH`, quyền filesystem và mạng.
  Câu này đã có ở docstring lane và author guide §10; đây là chỗ thứ ba, và ba
  chỗ đồng ý là cố ý — đây là tuyên bố dễ bị làm nhẹ đi nhất khi kể lại.
- **Ai được import**: admin (`user.is_admin`), một lần kiểm ở một chỗ.
- **Bốn trần** với lý do từng cái. `max_plugin_extracted_mb` là cái quan trọng và
  dễ quên: dung lượng nén không nói gì về thứ giải nén ghi ra.

Trần đặt rộng như An dặn: 50 MB zip · 500 member · 200 MB sau giải nén · 64 KB manifest.

### P1 — nhận và đăng ký, chưa chạy gì

- `POST /api/v1/algorithms/plugins` (multipart), `GET`, `GET {id}`, `PATCH {id}`.
  **Không có DELETE** — cùng lý do trang Models không có: một bundle là thứ một
  benchmark *đã chạy*.
- `inspect_bundle()` đọc mục lục: zip magic, member path an toàn, số member, tổng
  sau giải nén, đúng một `*/.planbench-plugin/plugin.json`, kích thước manifest,
  JSON hợp lệ, rồi `parse_manifest` của SDK.
- **Refusal của SDK trả nguyên văn.** Tác giả plugin gặp đúng câu mà CLI sẽ nói;
  viết lại cho dễ nghe là cho một người hai từ vựng cho cùng một lỗi.
- Bảng `plugin_bundles` + alembic `0010`. **Unique trên `(plugin_id,
  plugin_version)`**, không phải `(owner, name, version)` như bảng `models`: định
  danh candidate lấy từ manifest, nên hai upload cùng một phiên bản plugin là hai
  câu trả lời cho "cái gì tạo ra kết quả này".

**Một chỗ cố ý khác `models`:** bundle mà manifest không parse được thì **từ chối
luôn**, không lưu thành `FAILED`. Model có định danh từ form nên còn chỗ ghi lý
do; bundle lấy định danh từ manifest — không manifest thì không có `plugin_id`,
và bảng khoá trên nó sẽ đụng ngay upload hỏng thứ hai.

### P2 — giải nén và chạy thật

- `install_bundle()`: kiểm checksum trước khi giải, idempotent theo checksum,
  thay nguyên thư mục chứ không trộn.
- **Kiểm thoát thư mục lần thứ hai** lúc ghi file. P1 đã chặn tên xấu lúc đọc mục
  lục, nhưng chỉ kiểm ở thời điểm ghi mới biết file sẽ rơi vào đâu.
- Chạy `check_local_plugin` của SDK **qua lane subprocess**, deadline riêng 5 s

handle biến worker chết thành **safe stop**, tức một `LocalPlanResult` hợp lệ

"""VFH+ — a reactive histogram controller for the PlanBench host.

Implements the five stages of Ulrich & Borenstein's VFH+ (ICRA 1998):
a primary polar histogram built from enlarged obstacle bearings, a
binary histogram with hysteresis, a masked histogram that removes
directions the robot cannot steer into, candidate directions drawn from
the surviving openings, and a cost function that picks between them.

**Provenance, stated because a reader will otherwise assume otherwise.**
This was written from the published description of the algorithm, not
transcribed from the paper with the paper open. The five stages, their
order, and the cost function's form are the algorithm's; the constants
and two geometric simplifications named below are choices made here. It
has not been checked against the paper's own results, and a report
comparing it with numbers published for VFH+ would be comparing them
with this file.

What that does *not* affect: whether it runs, and whether the platform's
measurement of it is valid. Success rate, path length, clearance and
collisions are properties of the behaviour observed, whatever the
behaviour's pedigree.

Two places where a diff-drive robot forced a decision:

**Turning radius.** VFH+ masks directions using the circles the robot
would trace at full lock. A differential-drive robot's turning radius is
not fixed — it is ``v / w_max``, and at a standstill it is zero, so it
can spin in place and nothing is masked. That is modelled directly
rather than substituting a constant radius, which would forbid turns the
robot can actually make.

**Blocking test.** The paper sweeps limit angles outward from directly
behind the robot. This computes the same two limits by taking, on each
side, the nearest bearing whose obstacle intersects that side's turning
circle. Same quantity, arrived at without the sweep.

Deterministic by construction: no clock, no random number generator,
nothing that depends on how many times ``step`` has been called except
the two pieces of state the algorithm itself defines (the previous
binary histogram, for hysteresis, and the previously chosen direction,
which is a term in the cost function).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

LIDAR_2D = "lidar_2d"

#: The sector a direction falls in is found by rounding, so a bearing
#: exactly on a boundary must not oscillate between two sectors.
_EPS = 1e-9


class VFHPlusPlanner:
    """Local controller: histogram in, one velocity command out."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        sector_angle_deg: float = 5.0,
        safety_distance_m: float = 0.12,
        threshold_low: float = 0.55,
        threshold_high: float = 1.10,
        max_valley_sectors: int = 16,
        mu_target: float = 5.0,
        mu_heading: float = 2.0,
        mu_previous: float = 2.0,
        lookahead_m: float = 0.9,
        turn_gain: float = 2.2,
        speed_density_scale: float = 1.6,
        min_speed_fraction: float = 0.12,
    ) -> None:
        # mu1 > mu2 + mu3 is the paper's own constraint, and it is what
        # makes the controller commit to the goal rather than to its own
        # momentum. Refused here rather than clamped: a caller who set
        # these deliberately deserves to be told they cancel the
        # algorithm's intent, not to have it quietly restored.
        if mu_target <= mu_heading + mu_previous:
            raise ValueError(
                f"mu_target ({mu_target}) must exceed mu_heading + mu_previous "
                f"({mu_heading + mu_previous}); below that the controller prefers "
                "its current heading to the goal and orbits"
            )
        if threshold_low >= threshold_high:
            raise ValueError(
                f"threshold_low ({threshold_low}) must be below threshold_high "
                f"({threshold_high}); equal thresholds remove the hysteresis that "
                "separates VFH+ from VFH"
            )
        self._alpha = math.radians(sector_angle_deg)
        self._sectors = max(8, int(round(2.0 * math.pi / self._alpha)))
        # Recomputed from the sector count so alpha * sectors == 2*pi
        # exactly; a leftover fraction of a sector puts a seam in the
        # histogram that one bearing falls through.
        self._alpha = 2.0 * math.pi / self._sectors
        self._safety = safety_distance_m
        self._tau_low = threshold_low
        self._tau_high = threshold_high
        self._s_max = max(2, int(max_valley_sectors))
        self._mu = (mu_target, mu_heading, mu_previous)
        self._lookahead = lookahead_m
        self._turn_gain = turn_gain
        self._density_scale = speed_density_scale
        self._min_speed_fraction = min_speed_fraction

        self._binary: list[int] = [0] * self._sectors
        self._previous_sector: int | None = None
        self._path: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
        self._radius = 0.3
        self._v_max = 1.0
        self._w_max = 1.5

    # -- plugin contract -------------------------------------------------

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "vfh_plus"

    @property
    def control_period(self) -> float | None:
        """None: runs on every simulation step.

        VFH+ is a function of the current scan, so there is no rate below
        which it becomes wrong. Declaring a period here would ask the
        loop to hold a stale command for no reason the algorithm has.
        """
        return None

    def reset(self, request) -> None:
        self._path = [(float(p[0]), float(p[1])) for p in getattr(request, "global_path", ())]
        robot = dict(getattr(request, "robot", {}).get("robot_config") or {})
        self._radius = float(robot.get("radius", 0.3))
        self._v_max = float(robot.get("max_linear_velocity", 1.0))
        self._w_max = float(robot.get("max_angular_velocity", 1.5))
        # Episode state, cleared. A histogram carried across episodes
        # would let the previous map's walls bias the first tick of the
        # next one, and hysteresis is exactly the mechanism that would
        # carry it.
        self._binary = [0] * self._sectors
        self._previous_sector = None

    def step(self, request):
        state = dict(getattr(request, "state", {}).get("robot_state") or {})
        pose = dict(state.get("pose") or {})
        x = float(pose.get("x", 0.0))
        y = float(pose.get("y", 0.0))
        theta = float(pose.get("theta", 0.0))
        speed = float(state.get("linear_velocity", 0.0))

        ranges = _payload(request, LIDAR_2D)
        obstacles = _obstacle_bearings(ranges, theta)

        target = self._target_bearing(x, y, theta)
        primary = self._primary_histogram(obstacles)
        self._binary = self._binary_histogram(primary, self._binary)
        masked = self._masked_histogram(self._binary, obstacles, speed)

        chosen = self._choose_sector(masked, target, theta)
        if chosen is None:
            # Every direction blocked. Turning towards the target in
            # place is the one motion that cannot make contact, and it is
            # what recovers a robot that drove into a pocket.
            return {
                "linear_velocity": 0.0,
                "angular_velocity": _clamp(
                    self._turn_gain * _wrap(target), -self._w_max, self._w_max
                ),
            }

        self._previous_sector = chosen
        return self._command(chosen, primary, theta)

    # -- stage 1: primary polar histogram ---------------------------------

    def _primary_histogram(self, obstacles: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> list[float]:
        """Each return smeared over the sectors its enlarged width covers.

        ``m = c^2 (a - b d^2)`` with ``c = 1`` for a range return and
        ``a - b d_max^2 = 0``, which is the paper's constraint on the
        pair. Choosing ``a = 1`` on top of it puts the magnitude in
        ``[0, 1]`` per return, which is the scale the two thresholds are
        expressed in — the paper leaves that free.
        """
        histogram = [0.0] * self._sectors
        if not obstacles:
            return histogram
        d_max = max(distance for distance, _ in obstacles)
        if d_max <= 0.0:
            return histogram
        enlarged = self._radius + self._safety

        for distance, bearing in obstacles:
            magnitude = 1.0 - (distance * distance) / (d_max * d_max)
            if magnitude <= 0.0:
                continue
            # The half-angle the obstacle subtends once grown by the
            # robot's own footprint plus its safety margin. Inside that
            # radius there is no free direction left to compute, so the
            # obstacle blocks the whole half-plane it sits in.
            ratio = enlarged / distance if distance > 0.0 else 2.0
            gamma = math.asin(ratio) if ratio < 1.0 else math.pi / 2.0
            centre = self._sector_of(bearing)
            span = int(math.ceil(gamma / self._alpha))
            for offset in range(-span, span + 1):
                histogram[(centre + offset) % self._sectors] += magnitude
        return histogram

    # -- stage 2: binary polar histogram ----------------------------------

    def _binary_histogram(self, primary: list[float], previous: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        """Two thresholds, not one. This is what VFH+ adds to VFH.

        A single threshold makes a sector flicker between blocked and
        free as a reading crosses it, and the chosen direction flickers
        with it. Between the two thresholds the previous answer stands.
        """
        return [
            1
            if value > self._tau_high
            else 0
            if value < self._tau_low
            else previous[index]
            for index, value in enumerate(primary)
        ]

    # -- stage 3: masked polar histogram ----------------------------------

    def _masked_histogram(
        self, binary: list[int], obstacles: list[tuple[float, float]], speed: float
    ) -> list[int]:
        """Remove directions the robot cannot steer into from here.

        A sector can be empty and still unreachable: turning towards it
        would sweep the robot through something beside it. VFH+ models
        that with the circles traced at full lock.

        For a differential drive the radius is ``v / w_max``, so at rest
        it is zero and nothing is masked — correctly, because the robot
        can turn on the spot.
        """
        masked = list(binary)
        radius = abs(speed) / self._w_max if self._w_max > 0.0 else 0.0
        if radius <= _EPS:
            return masked

        enlarged = self._radius + self._safety
        limit_left = math.pi
        limit_right = -math.pi
        # Robot frame: +x is forward, +y is left. Left turn circle is
        # centred at (0, r), right turn circle at (0, -r).
        for distance, bearing in obstacles:
            relative = _wrap(bearing)
            ox = distance * math.cos(relative)
            oy = distance * math.sin(relative)
            blocks_left = math.hypot(ox, oy - radius) < radius + enlarged
            blocks_right = math.hypot(ox, oy + radius) < radius + enlarged
            if blocks_left and 0.0 < relative < limit_left:
                limit_left = relative
            if blocks_right and limit_right < relative < 0.0:
                limit_right = relative

        for index in range(self._sectors):
            bearing = self._bearing_of(index)
            if not (limit_right - _EPS <= bearing <= limit_left + _EPS):
                masked[index] = 1
        return masked

    # -- stages 4 and 5: candidates, cost, command ------------------------

    def _choose_sector(self, masked: list[int], target: float, theta: float) -> int | None:
        """Openings become candidate directions; the cost function ranks them."""
        openings = _openings(masked)
        if not openings:
            return None

        target_sector = self._sector_of(target)
        heading_sector = self._sector_of(0.0)
        previous = self._previous_sector if self._previous_sector is not None else target_sector

        candidates: list[int] = []
        for start, width in openings:
            if width >= self._s_max:
                # A wide opening offers three: hug either edge at a fixed
                # standoff, or drive straight at the target when it lies
                # inside. Steering at the middle of a wide corridor is the
                # answer VFH gave and the reason it took the long way
                # round obstacles it could have passed close to.
                half = self._s_max // 2
                candidates.append((start + half) % self._sectors)
                candidates.append((start + width - 1 - half) % self._sectors)
                if _within(target_sector, start, width, self._sectors):
                    candidates.append(target_sector)
            else:
                candidates.append((start + width // 2) % self._sectors)

        mu_target, mu_heading, mu_previous = self._mu
        best = None
        best_cost = math.inf
        for candidate in candidates:
            cost = (
                mu_target * self._sector_gap(candidate, target_sector)
                + mu_heading * self._sector_gap(candidate, heading_sector)
                + mu_previous * self._sector_gap(candidate, previous)
            )
            # Ties broken by the lower sector index rather than by
            # whichever the loop reached first: iteration order over
            # openings is stable, but relying on it makes the tie-break
            # invisible to a reader and fragile to a refactor.
            if cost < best_cost - _EPS or (abs(cost - best_cost) <= _EPS and candidate < best):
                best, best_cost = candidate, cost
        return best

    def _command(self, sector: int, primary: list[float], theta: float) -> dict[str, float]:
        """Speed falls with obstacle density ahead and with how hard we turn."""
        error = _wrap(self._bearing_of(sector))
        angular = _clamp(self._turn_gain * error, -self._w_max, self._w_max)

        density_ceiling = self._tau_high * self._density_scale
        density = min(primary[sector], density_ceiling)
        speed = self._v_max * (1.0 - density / density_ceiling) if density_ceiling > 0 else 0.0
        # Turning hard is itself a reason to slow down: the paper's second
        # reduction, and what stops the robot cutting a corner it is still
        # rotating away from.
        speed *= 1.0 - min(1.0, abs(angular) / self._w_max) if self._w_max > 0 else 1.0
        # A floor, because a controller that reaches exactly zero on a
        # crowded scan stops for good: nothing else moves the robot, so
        # the density that stopped it never changes.
        speed = max(speed, self._v_max * self._min_speed_fraction)
        return {"linear_velocity": speed, "angular_velocity": angular}

    # -- geometry helpers -------------------------------------------------

    def _target_bearing(self, x: float, y: float, theta: float) -> float:
        """Bearing to a carrot on the global path, in the robot's frame.

        The path is followed rather than the goal chased: aiming straight
        at the goal through a wall makes the histogram do the whole job
        and throws away the search that produced the path.
        """
        if not self._path:
            return 0.0
        nearest = min(
            range(len(self._path)),
            key=lambda index: math.hypot(self._path[index][0] - x, self._path[index][1] - y),
        )
        travelled = 0.0
        target = self._path[-1]
        for index in range(nearest, len(self._path) - 1):
            current = self._path[index]
            following = self._path[index + 1]
            travelled += math.hypot(following[0] - current[0], following[1] - current[1])
            if travelled >= self._lookahead:
                target = following
                break

"""VFH+ — a reactive histogram controller for the PlanBench host.

Implements the five stages of Ulrich & Borenstein's VFH+ (ICRA 1998):
a primary polar histogram built from enlarged obstacle bearings, a
binary histogram with hysteresis, a masked histogram that removes
directions the robot cannot steer into, candidate directions drawn from
the surviving openings, and a cost function that picks between them.

**Provenance, stated because a reader will otherwise assume otherwise.**
This was written from the published description of the algorithm, not
transcribed from the paper with the paper open. The five stages, their
order, and the cost function's form are the algorithm's; the constants
and two geometric simplifications named below are choices made here. It
has not been checked against the paper's own results, and a report
comparing it with numbers published for VFH+ would be comparing them
with this file.

What that does *not* affect: whether it runs, and whether the platform's
measurement of it is valid. Success rate, path length, clearance and
collisions are properties of the behaviour observed, whatever the
behaviour's pedigree.

Two places where a diff-drive robot forced a decision:

**Turning radius.** VFH+ masks directions using the circles the robot
would trace at full lock. A differential-drive robot's turning radius is
not fixed — it is ``v / w_max``, and at a standstill it is zero, so it
can spin in place and nothing is masked. That is modelled directly
rather than substituting a constant radius, which would forbid turns the
robot can actually make.

**Blocking test.** The paper sweeps limit angles outward from directly
behind the robot. This computes the same two limits by taking, on each
side, the nearest bearing whose obstacle intersects that side's turning
circle. Same quantity, arrived at without the sweep.

Deterministic by construction: no clock, no random number generator,
nothing that depends on how many times ``step`` has been called except
the two pieces of state the algorithm itself defines (the previous
binary histogram, for hysteresis, and the previously chosen direction,
which is a term in the cost function).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

LIDAR_2D = "lidar_2d"

#: The sector a direction falls in is found by rounding, so a bearing
#: exactly on a boundary must not oscillate between two sectors.
_EPS = 1e-9


class VFHPlusPlanner:
    """Local controller: histogram in, one velocity command out."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        sector_angle_deg: float = 5.0,
        safety_distance_m: float = 0.12,
        threshold_low: float = 0.55,
        threshold_high: float = 1.10,
        max_valley_sectors: int = 16,
        mu_target: float = 5.0,
        mu_heading: float = 2.0,
        mu_previous: float = 2.0,
        lookahead_m: float = 0.9,
        turn_gain: float = 2.2,
        speed_density_scale: float = 1.6,
        min_speed_fraction: float = 0.12,
    ) -> None:
        # mu1 > mu2 + mu3 is the paper's own constraint, and it is what
        # makes the controller commit to the goal rather than to its own
        # momentum. Refused here rather than clamped: a caller who set
        # these deliberately deserves to be told they cancel the
        # algorithm's intent, not to have it quietly restored.
        if mu_target <= mu_heading + mu_previous:
            raise ValueError(
                f"mu_target ({mu_target}) must exceed mu_heading + mu_previous "
                f"({mu_heading + mu_previous}); below that the controller prefers "
                "its current heading to the goal and orbits"
            )
        if threshold_low >= threshold_high:
            raise ValueError(
                f"threshold_low ({threshold_low}) must be below threshold_high "
                f"({threshold_high}); equal thresholds remove the hysteresis that "
                "separates VFH+ from VFH"
            )
        self._alpha = math.radians(sector_angle_deg)
        self._sectors = max(8, int(round(2.0 * math.pi / self._alpha)))
        # Recomputed from the sector count so alpha * sectors == 2*pi
        # exactly; a leftover fraction of a sector puts a seam in the
        # histogram that one bearing falls through.
        self._alpha = 2.0 * math.pi / self._sectors
        self._safety = safety_distance_m
        self._tau_low = threshold_low
        self._tau_high = threshold_high
        self._s_max = max(2, int(max_valley_sectors))
        self._mu = (mu_target, mu_heading, mu_previous)
        self._lookahead = lookahead_m
        self._turn_gain = turn_gain
        self._density_scale = speed_density_scale
        self._min_speed_fraction = min_speed_fraction

        self._binary: list[int] = [0] * self._sectors
        self._previous_sector: int | None = None
        self._path: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
        self._radius = 0.3
        self._v_max = 1.0
        self._w_max = 1.5

    # -- plugin contract -------------------------------------------------

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "vfh_plus"

    @property
    def control_period(self) -> float | None:
        """None: runs on every simulation step.

        VFH+ is a function of the current scan, so there is no rate below
        which it becomes wrong. Declaring a period here would ask the
        loop to hold a stale command for no reason the algorithm has.
        """
        return None

    def reset(self, request) -> None:
        self._path = [(float(p[0]), float(p[1])) for p in getattr(request, "global_path", ())]
        robot = dict(getattr(request, "robot", {}).get("robot_config") or {})
        self._radius = float(robot.get("radius", 0.3))
        self._v_max = float(robot.get("max_linear_velocity", 1.0))
        self._w_max = float(robot.get("max_angular_velocity", 1.5))
        # Episode state, cleared. A histogram carried across episodes
        # would let the previous map's walls bias the first tick of the
        # next one, and hysteresis is exactly the mechanism that would
        # carry it.
        self._binary = [0] * self._sectors
        self._previous_sector = None

    def step(self, request):
        state = dict(getattr(request, "state", {}).get("robot_state") or {})
        pose = dict(state.get("pose") or {})
        x = float(pose.get("x", 0.0))
        y = float(pose.get("y", 0.0))
        theta = float(pose.get("theta", 0.0))
        speed = float(state.get("linear_velocity", 0.0))

        ranges = _payload(request, LIDAR_2D)
        obstacles = _obstacle_bearings(ranges, theta)

        target = self._target_bearing(x, y, theta)
        primary = self._primary_histogram(obstacles)
        self._binary = self._binary_histogram(primary, self._binary)
        masked = self._masked_histogram(self._binary, obstacles, speed)

        chosen = self._choose_sector(masked, target, theta)
        if chosen is None:
            # Every direction blocked. Turning towards the target in
            # place is the one motion that cannot make contact, and it is
            # what recovers a robot that drove into a pocket.
            return {
                "linear_velocity": 0.0,
                "angular_velocity": _clamp(
                    self._turn_gain * _wrap(target), -self._w_max, self._w_max
                ),
            }

        self._previous_sector = chosen
        return self._command(chosen, primary, theta)

    # -- stage 1: primary polar histogram ---------------------------------

    def _primary_histogram(self, obstacles: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> list[float]:
        """Each return smeared over the sectors its enlarged width covers.

        ``m = c^2 (a - b d^2)`` with ``c = 1`` for a range return and
        ``a - b d_max^2 = 0``, which is the paper's constraint on the
        pair. Choosing ``a = 1`` on top of it puts the magnitude in
        ``[0, 1]`` per return, which is the scale the two thresholds are
        expressed in — the paper leaves that free.
        """
        histogram = [0.0] * self._sectors
        if not obstacles:
            return histogram
        d_max = max(distance for distance, _ in obstacles)
        if d_max <= 0.0:
            return histogram
        enlarged = self._radius + self._safety

        for distance, bearing in obstacles:
            magnitude = 1.0 - (distance * distance) / (d_max * d_max)
            if magnitude <= 0.0:
                continue
            # The half-angle the obstacle subtends once grown by the
            # robot's own footprint plus its safety margin. Inside that
            # radius there is no free direction left to compute, so the
            # obstacle blocks the whole half-plane it sits in.
            ratio = enlarged / distance if distance > 0.0 else 2.0
            gamma = math.asin(ratio) if ratio < 1.0 else math.pi / 2.0
            centre = self._sector_of(bearing)
            span = int(math.ceil(gamma / self._alpha))
            for offset in range(-span, span + 1):
                histogram[(centre + offset) % self._sectors] += magnitude
        return histogram

    # -- stage 2: binary polar histogram ----------------------------------

    def _binary_histogram(self, primary: list[float], previous: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        """Two thresholds, not one. This is what VFH+ adds to VFH.

        A single threshold makes a sector flicker between blocked and
        free as a reading crosses it, and the chosen direction flickers
        with it. Between the two thresholds the previous answer stands.
        """
        return [
            1
            if value > self._tau_high
            else 0
            if value < self._tau_low
            else previous[index]
            for index, value in enumerate(primary)
        ]

    # -- stage 3: masked polar histogram ----------------------------------

    def _masked_histogram(
        self, binary: list[int], obstacles: list[tuple[float, float]], speed: float
    ) -> list[int]:
        """Remove directions the robot cannot steer into from here.

        A sector can be empty and still unreachable: turning towards it
        would sweep the robot through something beside it. VFH+ models
        that with the circles traced at full lock.

        For a differential drive the radius is ``v / w_max``, so at rest
        it is zero and nothing is masked — correctly, because the robot
        can turn on the spot.
        """
        masked = list(binary)
        radius = abs(speed) / self._w_max if self._w_max > 0.0 else 0.0
        if radius <= _EPS:
            return masked

        enlarged = self._radius + self._safety
        limit_left = math.pi
        limit_right = -math.pi
        # Robot frame: +x is forward, +y is left. Left turn circle is
        # centred at (0, r), right turn circle at (0, -r).
        for distance, bearing in obstacles:
            relative = _wrap(bearing)
            ox = distance * math.cos(relative)
            oy = distance * math.sin(relative)
            blocks_left = math.hypot(ox, oy - radius) < radius + enlarged
            blocks_right = math.hypot(ox, oy + radius) < radius + enlarged
            if blocks_left and 0.0 < relative < limit_left:
                limit_left = relative
            if blocks_right and limit_right < relative < 0.0:
                limit_right = relative

        for index in range(self._sectors):
            bearing = self._bearing_of(index)
            if not (limit_right - _EPS <= bearing <= limit_left + _EPS):
                masked[index] = 1
        return masked

    # -- stages 4 and 5: candidates, cost, command ------------------------

    def _choose_sector(self, masked: list[int], target: float, theta: float) -> int | None:
        """Openings become candidate directions; the cost function ranks them."""
        openings = _openings(masked)
        if not openings:
            return None

        target_sector = self._sector_of(target)
        heading_sector = self._sector_of(0.0)
        previous = self._previous_sector if self._previous_sector is not None else target_sector

        candidates: list[int] = []
        for start, width in openings:
            if width >= self._s_max:
                # A wide opening offers three: hug either edge at a fixed
                # standoff, or drive straight at the target when it lies
                # inside. Steering at the middle of a wide corridor is the
                # answer VFH gave and the reason it took the long way
                # round obstacles it could have passed close to.
                half = self._s_max // 2
                candidates.append((start + half) % self._sectors)
                candidates.append((start + width - 1 - half) % self._sectors)
                if _within(target_sector, start, width, self._sectors):
                    candidates.append(target_sector)
            else:
                candidates.append((start + width // 2) % self._sectors)

        mu_target, mu_heading, mu_previous = self._mu
        best = None
        best_cost = math.inf
        for candidate in candidates:
            cost = (
                mu_target * self._sector_gap(candidate, target_sector)
                + mu_heading * self._sector_gap(candidate, heading_sector)
                + mu_previous * self._sector_gap(candidate, previous)
            )
            # Ties broken by the lower sector index rather than by
            # whichever the loop reached first: iteration order over
            # openings is stable, but relying on it makes the tie-break
            # invisible to a reader and fragile to a refactor.
            if cost < best_cost - _EPS or (abs(cost - best_cost) <= _EPS and candidate < best):
                best, best_cost = candidate, cost
        return best

    def _command(self, sector: int, primary: list[float], theta: float) -> dict[str, float]:
        """Speed falls with obstacle density ahead and with how hard we turn."""
        error = _wrap(self._bearing_of(sector))
        angular = _clamp(self._turn_gain * error, -self._w_max, self._w_max)

        density_ceiling = self._tau_high * self._density_scale
        density = min(primary[sector], density_ceiling)
        speed = self._v_max * (1.0 - density / density_ceiling) if density_ceiling > 0 else 0.0
        # Turning hard is itself a reason to slow down: the paper's second
        # reduction, and what stops the robot cutting a corner it is still
        # rotating away from.
        speed *= 1.0 - min(1.0, abs(angular) / self._w_max) if self._w_max > 0 else 1.0
        # A floor, because a controller that reaches exactly zero on a
        # crowded scan stops for good: nothing else moves the robot, so
        # the density that stopped it never changes.
        speed = max(speed, self._v_max * self._min_speed_fraction)
        return {"linear_velocity": speed, "angular_velocity": angular}

    # -- geometry helpers -------------------------------------------------

    def _target_bearing(self, x: float, y: float, theta: float) -> float:
        """Bearing to a carrot on the global path, in the robot's frame.

        The path is followed rather than the goal chased: aiming straight
        at the goal through a wall makes the histogram do the whole job
        and throws away the search that produced the path.
        """

            return 0.0
        nearest = min(
            range(len(self._path)),
            key=lambda index: math.hypot(self._path[index][0] - x, self._path[index][1] - y),
        )
        travelled = 0.0
        target = self._path[-1]
        for index in range(nearest, len(self._path) - 1):
            current = self._path[index]
            following = self._path[index + 1]
            travelled += math.hypot(following[0] - current[0], following[1] - current[1])
            if travelled >= self._lookahead:
                target = following
                break
        return _wrap(math.atan2(target[1] - y, target[0] - x) - theta)

    def _sector_of(self, bearing: float) -> int:
        return int((_wrap(bearing) + math.pi) / self._alpha) % self._sectors

    def _bearing_of(self, sector: int) -> float:
        return _wrap(-math.pi + (sector + 0.5) * self._alpha)

    def _sector_gap(self, a: int, b: int) -> int:
        """Distance between two sectors the short way round the circle."""
        gap = abs(a - b) % self._sectors
        return min(gap, self._sectors - gap)


# -- module helpers -------------------------------------------------------


def _payload(request, capability: str):
    """The granted channel, or a refusal naming what was missing.

    Raising rather than returning an empty scan: the host turns this into
    a safe stop recorded in the trace, while an empty scan would let the

    Wraps around the seam at the back of the robot: an opening that
    straddles it is one opening, and treating it as two would put a
    spurious edge behind the robot for the cost function to prefer.

    return runs

    return ((sector - start) % total) < width

    return math.atan2(math.sin(angle), math.cos(angle))

        two thresholds are expressed on that scale. The paper leaves

        builds its histogram from a window of cells around the robot
        rather than from everything the sensor can see, and the
        distinction is not cosmetic here: normalising by a 5 m range
        leaves a wall 2 m away with a magnitude of 0.84, so a corridor
        reads as blocked in every direction. Returns past the window are
        dropped rather than down-weighted, which is what "outside the
        window" means.

        **A sector takes the strongest return covering it, not the sum of
        them.** The paper sums certainty values from an occupancy grid,
        where summing means accumulated *evidence* that something is
        there. A LiDAR return is already certain, so summing over rays

# VFH+ bundle for PlanBench

Ready to import: upload **`vfh_plus.zip`** through **Models → Import algorithm**
(admin only). Everything else here is source and notes.

```
vfh_plus_import/
  vfh_plus.zip                     <- the file to upload
  vfh_plus/                        <- what is inside it
    __init__.py
    planner.py
    .planbench-plugin/plugin.json
  DESCRIPTION.txt                  <- paste into the form's Description field
  README.md                        <- this file
  MAPPING.md                       <- each function against the paper's stages
```

---

## 1. What this is, and what it is not

An implementation of VFH+ (Ulrich & Borenstein, ICRA 1998) **written from the
published description of the algorithm, not transcribed with the paper open.**

The five stages, their order, and the cost function's form are the algorithm's.
The constants, and the four decisions listed in §3, are choices made here. It has
not been checked against the paper's own results.

**What that affects: the label, not the numbers.** "This controller reached the
goal in 8 of 10 scenarios" is a fact about the behaviour observed and is true
whoever wrote it. "VFH+ reached the goal in 8 of 10" is a different claim and
needs the code to be VFH+. If this goes into a decision report next to DWA, the
report has to say which of the two it is claiming — the same rule
`_RRT_STAR_DESCRIPTION` already applies to the cost-aware RRT\* in this
repository.

Paste `DESCRIPTION.txt` into the form's Description field so the sentence travels
with the bundle instead of living only here.

## 2. Measured before packaging

Ten library scenarios, one seed (`episode_seed=1`), 45 s timeout, default
parameters, driven through `run_stack` — the same loop a benchmark uses.

| Scenario | This bundle | `astar+dwa` (`dwa_balanced`) |
|---|---|---|
| doorway | success (171) | success (174) |
| narrow_corridor | success (260) | stuck |
| wide_corridor | success (256) | success (254) |
| static_obstacles | success (227) | success (198) |
| open_space | success (192) | success (194) |
| bidirectional_corridor | **collision** | stuck |
| crossing_obstacle | success (237) | success (234) |
| intersection | success (256) | success (254) |
| sudden_stop | success (299) | stuck |
| dynamic_warehouse | **collision** | collision |
| | **8/10** | **6/10** |

**One seed is not a result.** It is a smoke test: it says the bundle runs, drives
and terminates. Every scenario here has one dynamic-obstacle realisation, and the
platform's paired bootstrap over many seeds exists precisely because a table like
this one is noise. Do not quote it.

**Both failures are collisions with moving obstacles, and that is the algorithm
rather than the implementation.** VFH+ is purely reactive: it has no model of
obstacle motion, so it steers around where an obstacle *is* and not where it is
going. The repository already measured what that costs — `dwa_predictive` was
built to close exactly this gap and was withdrawn because the perception feeding
it could not (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS L16, L19).

## 3. Where this departs from a literal reading

Each of these was forced by measurement, and each is written up at the function
that makes it. `MAPPING.md` names the stage every one belongs to.

**A sector takes the nearest return covering it, not the sum of them.** The paper
sums certainty values from an occupancy grid, where summing means accumulated
*evidence*. A LiDAR return is already certain, so summing counts one wall once per
ray that struck it: with 72 rays each spread over about eleven sectors, the first
version marked 85% of directions blocked while standing in open space.

**The active window is 2.5 m, not the sensor's 5 m range.** VFH+ builds its
histogram from a window around the robot. Normalising by the full range leaves a
wall 2 m away with magnitude 0.84, so a corridor reads as blocked in every
direction.

**The window shrinks to the goal when the goal is nearer.** A goal against a wall
is otherwise unreachable: the wall behind it blocks the direction the goal is in,
and the robot circles in front of its own destination — `wide_corridor` spent 861
steps doing that.

**Forward speed is gated on alignment and on the sector straight ahead.** VFH+
selects a *direction*; a differential drive cannot move in one until it has turned
to face it. Commanding speed while the selection sits 90° away drives the robot
into whatever is actually ahead, which is how `narrow_corridor` ended up holding
0.5 m/s against a wall.

Plus one adaptation that is not a departure so much as an instantiation: the
masking turning radius is `v / w_max`, because a differential drive has no fixed
minimum radius and can spin in place at rest.

## 4. Parameters

All of `config_schema` maps to a constructor argument, so anything here can be set
per candidate without touching the code.

| Name | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `sector_angle_deg` | 5.0 | histogram resolution; 72 sectors |
| `safety_distance_m` | 0.12 | added to the robot radius when enlarging obstacles |
| `active_window_m` | 2.5 | how far ahead the histogram decides |
| `threshold_low` / `threshold_high` | 0.30 / 0.55 | hysteresis pair; magnitudes are in [0, 1] |
| `max_valley_sectors` | 16 | above this an opening is wide and offers edge candidates |
| `mu_target` / `mu_heading` / `mu_previous` | 5.0 / 2.0 / 2.0 | cost weights; **the constructor refuses `mu_target <= mu_heading + mu_previous`**, which is the paper's own constraint |
| `lookahead_m` | 0.9 | carrot distance along the global path |
| `turn_gain` | 2.2 | proportional gain from bearing error to angular velocity |
| `speed_density_scale` | 1.6 | density at which speed reaches zero, as a multiple of `threshold_high` |
| `min_speed_fraction` | 0.12 | creep speed, applied only where forward travel is permitted |

`control_period` is added by the host, not by this bundle: it is the deployment's
cycle time and the deadline the subprocess lane enforces.

## 5. Re-importing after a change

The registry keys a bundle on `(plugin_id, plugin_version)`, so importing the same
version twice is refused. Change the code, **bump `version` in `plugin.json`**,
re-zip, import again. The candidate identity follows the archive's checksum, so
the new bundle is a new candidate and the old results keep pointing at the code
that produced them.

Zip the **directory**, not its contents:

```sh
cd vfh_plus_import && zip -r vfh_plus.zip vfh_plus
```

**One seed is not a result.** It is a smoke test: it says the bundle runs, drives
and terminates. Every scenario here has one dynamic-obstacle realisation, and the
platform's paired bootstrap over many seeds exists precisely because a table like
this one is noise. Do not quote it.

**Both failures are collisions with moving obstacles, and that is the algorithm
rather than the implementation.** VFH+ is purely reactive: it has no model of
obstacle motion, so it steers around where an obstacle *is* and not where it is
going. The repository already measured what that costs — `dwa_predictive` was
built to close exactly this gap and was withdrawn because the perception feeding
it could not (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS L16, L19).

## 3. Where this departs from a literal reading

Each of these was forced by measurement, and each is written up at the function
that makes it. `MAPPING.md` names the stage every one belongs to.

**A sector takes the nearest return covering it, not the sum of them.** The paper
sums certainty values from an occupancy grid, where summing means accumulated
*evidence*. A LiDAR return is already certain, so summing counts one wall once per
ray that struck it: with 72 rays each spread over about eleven sectors, the first
version marked 85% of directions blocked while standing in open space.

**The active window is 2.5 m, not the sensor's 5 m range.** VFH+ builds its
histogram from a window around the robot. Normalising by the full range leaves a
wall 2 m away with magnitude 0.84, so a corridor reads as blocked in every
direction.

**The window shrinks to the goal when the goal is nearer.** A goal against a wall
is otherwise unreachable: the wall behind it blocks the direction the goal is in,
and the robot circles in front of its own destination — `wide_corridor` spent 861
steps doing that.

**Forward speed is gated on alignment and on the sector straight ahead.** VFH+
selects a *direction*; a differential drive cannot move in one until it has turned
to face it. Commanding speed while the selection sits 90° away drives the robot
into whatever is actually ahead, which is how `narrow_corridor` ended up holding
0.5 m/s against a wall.

masking turning radius is `v / w_max`, because a differential drive has no fixed
minimum radius and can spin in place at rest.

All of `config_schema` maps to a constructor argument, so anything here can be set
per candidate without touching the code.

| Name | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `sector_angle_deg` | 5.0 | histogram resolution; 72 sectors |
| `safety_distance_m` | 0.12 | added to the robot radius when enlarging obstacles |
| `active_window_m` | 2.5 | how far ahead the histogram decides |
| `threshold_low` / `threshold_high` | 0.30 / 0.55 | hysteresis pair; magnitudes are in [0, 1] |
| `max_valley_sectors` | 16 | above this an opening is wide and offers edge candidates |
| `mu_target` / `mu_heading` / `mu_previous` | 5.0 / 2.0 / 2.0 | cost weights; **the constructor refuses `mu_target <= mu_heading + mu_previous`**, which is the paper's own constraint |
| `lookahead_m` | 0.9 | carrot distance along the global path |
| `turn_gain` | 2.2 | proportional gain from bearing error to angular velocity |
| `speed_density_scale` | 1.6 | density at which speed reaches zero, as a multiple of `threshold_high` |
| `min_speed_fraction` | 0.12 | creep speed, applied only where forward travel is permitted |

`control_period` is added by the host, not by this bundle: it is the deployment's
cycle time and the deadline the subprocess lane enforces.

The registry keys a bundle on `(plugin_id, plugin_version)`, so importing the same
version twice is refused. Change the code, **bump `version` in `plugin.json`**,
re-zip, import again. The candidate identity follows the archive's checksum, so
the new bundle is a new candidate and the old results keep pointing at the code
that produced them.

```
